protocol_name: Flow-focusing dye demo (reference board, not the pipeline's encapsulator)

sizing.capsule_count_note: not in chip spec; sheet default 100,000 used

scenario.description: No scenario file: the sim adapter records the commands the planner sent and nothing else. No virtual chip, no sensors and no injected faults, so there is no reality to configure - and nothing was measured, which is why simulated_hardware is true.

events.narration: Prime the board with oil before anything aqueous goes in. Do this first and always: the walls have to be oil-wetted for water-in-oil to work at all, and an aqueous stream that touches a dry wall first will wet it and keep wetting it. Getting this order right, and seeing what happens when you do not, is half the point of running the board. This is a FILL, not a sweep: the board arrives dry, so there is nothing in delay_1 to clear and no exchange target to reach - the step just has to displace air. One lane volume, 4.68 uL, is what the serpentine holds; the junctions and channels upstream of it add about 3.62 uL, so in practice you keep pushing until oil comes out of out_caps and no timer decides it. Sized at 21.5 uL (the chamber's old bounding-box volume_ul) this step claimed to put four and a half lane volumes of oil into a 4.68 uL lane.

Start the two dye streams and the oil, and let the junction settle. Expect a minute or two of ragged, uneven droplets before it locks into a steady drip: that is normal, and it is the syringe pump and the tubing settling rather than the chip. NO CELLS GO ON THIS BOARD - both aqueous streams are dye, because this is a geometry demo and not the pipeline's encapsulator. The orifice is 300 um wide by 150 um deep, so droplets are confined by the depth: treat 150 um as an INDICATIVE bound, not a prediction. At about 0.13 droplets per second the demo batch of 79 droplets takes about 10 min.

FILM THIS. The serpentine shows the droplet train. MEASURE THE SPREAD, NOT THE DIAMETER: even spacing and even size is the whole result, and the 150 um figure is only the depth bound. If droplets vary in size the flow ratio is off; if they merge the surfactant or the surface treatment is wrong.

Collect into a tube and look at the droplets under a scope. NOTHING IS CURED AND NOTHING GOES DOWNSTREAM: these are dye droplets of order 150 um from a geometry demo, not the pipeline's 70 um capsules. Those come from the off-chip commercial droplet kit and its 40 um nozzle, because a 40 um orifice is 5x below our 200 um in-plane fabrication floor and cannot be made here.
